name: Haiku global diversification via US-listed ADRs and ETFs
strategy: Broad S&P 500 core with international and energy exposure, rotated from concentrated dividend-yield positions to capture Q4 market participation while maintaining income and defensive positioning
reassessment_note: Round 3 is severely underperforming SPY at +0.52% versus +3.80%, driven by concentrated dividend-yield positions that are broadly underwater (XLF -7.80%, VTV -3.73%, EFA -3.77%, KRE -4.78%, TLT -5.41%). Original strategy intended 'tactical short on QQQ following exhaustion' but this was never implemented; however, QQQ remains near 52-week highs and mega-cap tech concentration is extreme (93% of S&P gains from 5 names). Rather than fighting momentum with a short into ongoing strength, pivoting to core market exposure via SPY to capture broad participation while maintaining outperformers (XLE at +21.6% YTD despite current flatness, EWJ at +21.58% YTD), diversified dividend harvest via SCHD and VYM (broader than failed single-sector approach), and defensive bond ballast via AGG. Increased cash to 17% for rebalancing flexibility. This maintains novelty rule compliance (EWJ overlap only; well below 50% threshold vs Round 2).

positions.thesis: Core S&P 500 exposure to capture broad market participation in Q4 rally momentum. Direct participation in the 2.78% YTD advance without sector concentration. Stop-loss at 12% protects against sharp equity drawdowns; take-profit at 30% locks in strong rally gains if market continues.

Energy sector outperformer with +21.6% YTD return. Current near-flat position (+0.13%) likely undervalued given strong oil fundamentals (prices above $103/bbl due to Middle East maritime friction). Oil majors provide cash-flow resilience and commodity upside.
Japan equity with proven momentum at +21.58% YTD and +4.30% current return. Provides geographic and currency diversification from US mega-cap tech concentration while maintaining positive trend.

Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF provides diversified dividend income across market-cap spectrum, superior to concentrated single-sector XLF or XLV approach. Maintains dividend-harvest philosophy while reducing single-sector risk that drove underperformance.

Broad investment-grade bond ETF provides defensive ballast, interest income, and portfolio stabilization against equity volatility. Protects against sharp drawdowns while participating in broader portfolio gains.

Healthcare sector allocation reduced from previous 14% to manage downside (-4.51% current). Sector provides dividend yield and diversification from tech concentration. Smaller position reflects current weakness while maintaining exposure to defensive healthcare fundamentals.

Vanguard High Dividend Yield ETF provides market-cap-weighted high-yield alternative to single-sector dividend plays. Diversified income generation across sectors while reducing concentration risk from failed dividend-stock strategy.
